issues.t: Cracked plastic panel below the liftgate window
issues.sym: A crack spreads across the plastic trim panel under the rear glass, often near the Lincoln badge or handle. Some owners find water getting in.
issues.why: The liftgate applique is plastic and cracks with age and stress; worn liftgate glass hinges can let the glass knock against it. Ford published a service procedure for the cracked applique.
issues.next: Replace the panel before water reaches the latch and wiring. An aftermarket panel and a body shop are usually cheaper than a dealer.

issues.t: Burned or leaking valves causing misfire
issues.sym: Hesitation when accelerating, rough idle, a flashing check engine light, a failed emissions test, or exhaust smell.
issues.why: Owners report burned or leaking valves on one or more cylinders of the 4.6L V8, which drops compression and causes a steady misfire.
issues.next: Have a compression or leak-down test done to confirm a valve problem before replacing coils or plugs. Cylinder head repair is usually needed.

issues.t: Ignition coil misfires
issues.sym: A check engine light with misfire codes, shaking at idle, or stumbling under load, often worse in damp weather.
issues.why: The coil-on-plug ignition coils on the 4.6L V8 crack and fail. Ford issued misfire bulletins and extended warranty coverage on the coils for these years; that coverage has likely run out.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read and swap the coil on the misfiring cylinder to confirm. Replace spark plugs at the same time if they are due.

issues.t: Automatic transmission failure
issues.sym: Slipping, flaring revs between gears, harsh shifts, lost gears, or no movement.
issues.why: The 5-speed automatic in these SUVs wears internally; transmission problems are among the most-reported complaints for this generation.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it slips or will not engage, get a transmission diagnosis before more damage is done.

issues.t: Delayed or harsh engagement into Reverse
issues.sym: A long pause or a hard clunk when shifting into Reverse, mostly when the transmission is cold.
issues.why: Ford bulletins cover this on the 5R55S automatic. Some trucks got fluid that was blended wrong, and Ford ran a program that added a fluid additive.
issues.next: Ask a shop to check the bulletins (TSB 05612 and program 04B22). A fluid service or valve body repair is the usual fix.

issues.t: Shift cable can pop off and show the wrong gear (recall)
issues.sym: The gear shown on the dash does not match the real gear, or the shifter feels loose.
issues.why: The shift cable can come out of its bracket, so the transmission may not be in the gear the driver selected.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 02V-313 and always set the parking brake.

issues.t: Shifter stuck in Park or broken shift linkage
issues.sym: The shift lever will not move out of Park, or it moves freely without changing gears.
issues.why: A failed brake switch can keep the shifter locked, and the shift rod or linkage can break.
issues.next: Check whether the brake lights work, which points to the brake switch. If they do, have the shifter and linkage inspected.

issues.t: Rear wheel bearing hum or growl
issues.sym: A hum or growl from the rear that gets louder with speed and may change when turning.
issues.why: The rear wheel bearings wear out; Ford issued a bulletin about noise from the hub bearings.
issues.next: Have the bearings checked before they get loose. A badly worn bearing can affect handling and the ABS sensor.

issues.t: Transmission fluid leak at the cooler
issues.sym: Red fluid dripping near the front of the SUV, or low transmission fluid.
issues.why: Ford bulletin TSB 17563 covers a fluid leak at the transmission cooler or its lines.
issues.next: Fix the leak quickly; running the transmission low on fluid can ruin it.

issues.t: A/C stops blowing cold
issues.sym: The air conditioning blows warm, only one side cools, or it needs frequent recharging.
issues.why: Refrigerant leaks and climate system faults are reported, and some owners face large repair bills.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested before adding refrigerant again; fixing the leak is cheaper than repeat recharges.

issues.t: Rear defroster lines stop working
issues.sym: The rear window will not clear, some heater lines stay foggy, or AM radio reception is poor.
issues.why: The defroster grid lines and the terminal tabs on the glass break; the radio antenna is part of the same grid.
issues.next: A shop can repair broken grid lines or terminal tabs with a repair kit instead of replacing the glass.

issues.t: Intake valves can break and cause engine failure (recall)
issues.sym: Misfiring, rough running, loud knocking, or a sudden loss of power.
issues.why: Some 3.0L twin-turbo V6 engines have intake valves that can break, which can destroy the engine.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-635. If the engine starts knocking or running rough, pull over and have it towed.

issues.t: Plug-in hybrid battery cell can short and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Possibly a battery warning or reduced charge. In rare cases, smoke or fire from the high-voltage battery.
issues.why: A defect in a high-voltage battery cell can cause an internal short. Some earlier repairs were done wrong, so a second recall followed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 23V-626 and 25V-349. Follow any charging limits in the recall letter and park outside until it is fixed.

issues.t: Backup or 360-degree camera image fails (several recalls)
issues.sym: The rear or 360-degree camera shows a blank, flickering, flipped or frozen image, or it stays on after reversing.
issues.why: Image processing module software and hardware faults, and even phone interference, can disrupt the camera feed. Ford has issued many recalls and repeat fixes.
issues.next: Look up your VIN for every open camera recall and have them all done. Use mirrors and look over your shoulder until then.

issues.t: Park pawl may engage while moving (recall)
issues.sym: A loud bang or grinding while driving slowly, or the SUV rolling after being shifted to Park.
issues.why: The transmission can engage its Park lock while the vehicle is still moving, which damages the parking mechanism.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 26V-402 and set the parking brake every time you park.

issues.t: Second-row easy-entry seat can unlatch or tip (recalls)
issues.sym: A second-row seat folds, slides or tips forward unexpectedly, or does not lock firmly.
issues.why: The easy-entry switch on the outer second-row seats can bind and leave the seat unlatched.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 25V-393 and 26V-451. Make sure the seat is locked before anyone sits in it.

issues.t: Second-row seat belt anchor bolts may be loose (recalls)
issues.sym: Usually no symptoms. In a crash a seat belt may not hold properly.
issues.why: Bolts that anchor the seat belt buckles and retractors may not have been tightened properly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 25V-093 and 26V-159 and have the bolts inspected for free.

issues.t: Low-pressure fuel pump can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Hard starting, sputtering, loss of power, or the engine stalling while driving.
issues.why: The low-pressure fuel pump in the tank can fail.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-455. If it stalls, get off the road safely and have it towed.

issues.t: Windshield wiper motor can fail (recall)
issues.sym: Wipers stop, slow down or park in the wrong position, often in heavy rain.
issues.why: The front wiper motor can fail, leaving the driver unable to clear the windshield.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 26V-117 and have the motor inspected.

issues.t: Knock or thump from the left cylinder head
issues.sym: A knock or thump from the top of the engine on the driver side.
issues.why: Ford service message SSM 51665 covers this noise on 2021-2023 vehicles with the 2.7L or 3.0L engine.
issues.next: Have a Lincoln dealer inspect it while the vehicle is under warranty.

issues.t: Rear driveshaft weld may crack (recall)
issues.sym: Vibration or clunking from under the car, then possible loss of drive.
issues.why: The driveshaft can fracture along its weld seam, which can cause loss of drive, roll-away in Park, or damage to the fuel tank.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 20V-693 and use the parking brake.

issues.t: Rear lower control arm bolts may break (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from the rear, a wandering feel, or poor alignment.
issues.why: Some rear lower control arm bolts were not heat-treated and can break, reducing steering control.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 21V-154 and have the bolts replaced.

issues.t: Tires wear out early
issues.sym: Tires need replacing around 20,000-25,000 miles, sometimes with uneven wear.
issues.why: Owners report fast tire wear on this heavy, powerful SUV with large performance tires.
issues.next: Rotate tires every 5,000 miles and check alignment if wear is uneven.

issues.t: Rear door window trim can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Wind noise, rattles, or trim lifting from the rear door window frame or rear pillar.
issues.why: The window bars and pillar trim may not be glued on well enough and can come off.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-407. If a piece is loose, tape it or remove it before driving at speed.

issues.t: Fuel filler tube may come loose in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms in normal driving.
issues.why: The fuel filler tube may separate in a crash, which could leak fuel.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 22V-088 and get the free repair.

issues.t: Front frame rails may be too weak (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms in normal driving.
issues.why: The engine compartment rails may not have been heat-treated correctly, reducing crash protection.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 22V-454.

issues.t: Loose bolt may stop Park from engaging (recall)
issues.sym: The SUV rolls even though the shifter shows Park.
issues.why: A loose bolt inside the transmission can keep the Park mechanism from working.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V-070 and always set the parking brake until fixed.

issues.t: Trailer hitch bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the hitch when towing, or a hitch that moves.
issues.why: Bolts holding the factory trailer hitch may not be tight, so a trailer could come loose.
issues.next: Do not tow until recall 25V-687 has been checked on your VIN.

issues.t: Transmission valve body machining error (recall)
issues.sym: No Reverse, or the vehicle moving unexpectedly.
issues.why: The transmission valve body may have been machined incorrectly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-164 and get the free repair.

issues.t: Transmission crossmember bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from under the car, vibration, or loss of drive power.
issues.why: Loose crossmember bolts can leave the transmission poorly supported.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-020.

issues.t: Windshield may have air bubbles (recall)
issues.sym: Bubbles or flaws in the windshield glass that blur the view.
issues.why: Some windshields were made with air bubbles in the glass.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-730 and get the free windshield replacement.

issues.t: Driver seat may recline on its own (recall)
issues.sym: The empty driver seat moves backward without anyone touching the controls.
issues.why: The driver seat can recline unintentionally, which could trap a second-row passenger.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 26V-470 and keep second-row legs clear of the seat back.

issues.t: Climate system failure can disable the defroster (recall)
issues.sym: The heat, defrost and defog stop working, so the windshield fogs or ices.
issues.why: An HVAC fault can disable windshield defrosting.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 26V-202 and do not drive if you cannot clear the windshield.
